content.comment_body: I have a codebase from about twelve years ago which was originally written for older [product_name] hardware ([article_no] hardware type). When attempting to load this code into a newer [product_name] module using [product_name] V8.3, I receive an error stating: 'Transfer not possible because the connected device is incompatible. Refer to the device selection dialog for supported devices.' Loading a freshly created program works fine. Copying and pasting blocks from the original code to a new project causes a warning about unavailable function blocks, including a length of the problematic blocks. It appears these blocks are deprecated. Is there a solution other than rewriting the entire program? The concern is that several units in the field rely on this obsolete hardware, and I'm trying to find a compatible replacement that can run the original code. For reference, my background is in embedded systems but I'm tackling this as the PLC team is currently unavailable.

It's challenging to assist without specific details about your program or which blocks are unsupported. There isn't a universal method for converting every legacy program to newer [product_name] controllers. Regards, [user_name]
Thank you [user_name]. I raised this issue internally, but my employer doesn't permit sharing proprietary code online.

I understand the challenge with sharing internal company code. I'm unable to provide my organization's programs either. You could upload screenshots showing detailed error messages without revealing code, which might be helpful. If that's insufficient, you may need to handle the conversion process yourself. Sorry. Regards, [user_name]
If you possess the newer [product_name] V8.3 ([article_no]), the correct hardware selection should be [product_name] V8.3 rather than [article_no].

Hi [user_name], When I open the original software in [product_name] V8.3, the hardware tab only offers [article_no] Standard and [article_no] Standard, with other options greyed out. I'll likely reach out to the local [company_name] distributor to explore replacement options.
I'm unable to understand the issue without more context. Could you upload your original program as a ZIP archive?
Hi [user_name], That's not really an option. My employer isn't comfortable with sharing code online. I'll contact [company_name] or their representative for advice. Thanks for your help.
You can send the ZIP file via private message so it remains confidential.

If I recall correctly, you may be able to select a greyed-out hardware type to convert the program. This will generate detailed messages identifying which code cannot be converted. This could be useful. Regards, [user_name]

Hi [user_name], When I try clicking on the greyed-out options, I see messages such as: B002/1: Input inversion not supported. Or alternatively: [product_name] 8.3 softkey parameter width is not suitable.
It seems this is a bug with [product_name] V8.3.
On the German section of the forum, a user encountered this issue recently and contacted Support. This was the response:
So should I download V8.2 and proceed from there?
There is no download available for the previous [product_name] V8.2, only for the current version 8.3. Would you be able to send the program via private message?
Hi [user_name], Unfortunately, that's not possible. My employer insists that versions of the code are not shared online. It's quite frustrating. Thanks for your willingness to help.
Without access to [product_name] V8.2, there aren't any viable options. I just wanted to assist, nothing else.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encounter compatibility challenges when transferring older code written for legacy [product_name] hardware onto newer modules through [product_name] V8.3. The software blocks the transfer due to hardware incompatibility and highlights unsupported or deprecated function blocks. Some hardware types are unavailable for selection, restricting users from easily updating or migrating legacy installations. This creates difficulty in maintaining and upgrading existing field units using outdated hardware.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect either backward compatibility or an easy migration process that allows older programs to run on updated hardware without significant modification. The goal is to make use of existing code with minimal effort.
